question:
A 3-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department by his parents due to a 4-hour history of
hand pain. His mother reports that the pain has only slightly improved with ibuprofen. He has no prior
history of similar episodes. The child was born at term and has otherwise been healthy. His family
moved to the United States from Equatorial Guinea 2 years ago. On examination, he appears to be in
acute distress. His temperature is 38.2ºC (100.8ºF), pulse is 114/min, and respirations are 30/min. The
fingers of both hands are tender, warm, erythematous, and edematous. The rest of the examination is
unremarkable. What is the most appropriate initial diagnostic test? Answer Choices: (A) Peripheral
blood smear (B) Blood culture (C) X-ray of the hands (D) Joint aspiration and culture (E) Nailfold
capillary microscopy (F) Serum ferritin levels (G) Complete blood count with differential (H) Serum uric
acid level (I) Hemoglobin electrophoresis (J) C-reactive protein measurement
 A. Joint aspiration and culture
B. Blood culture
C. Serum uric acid level
D. Hemoglobin electrophoresis
E. Complete blood count with differential
F. Nailfold capillary microscopy
G. Serum ferritin levels
H. X-ray of the hands
I. Peripheral blood smear
J. C-reactive protein measurement
